findings.issue: OWASP A01 Broken Access Control / IDOR: resumeOnCallback could otherwise advance another subscriber's execution from a forged callback_data.
findings.suggestion: Verified mitigated: claimForCallback CAS predicate is scoped by subscriberId (_id AND subscriberId AND status==waiting_for_reply AND stepRunStatus==pending). A forged executionId belonging to a foreign subscriber fails the predicate -> null -> no-op. Atomic, server-side. Covered by resumeOnCallback_rejects_foreign_subscriber IT.

No user input flows into callback_data: it is server-minted ObjectId-hex execution id + ':' + loop index. No injection surface. URL buttons carry the url verbatim into reply_markup but Telegram renders client-side; the backend never dereferences (no SSRF). URL scheme validation is Task 4's activate-time concern.
All new log lines (MENU_PARKED, RESUME_CALLBACK, STEP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, BROKEN_CURSOR) carry only ids/funnelId/codes -- no rendered text, button labels, or callback_data payload. No PII leakage.

findings.issue: DoS via infinite graph loop (button back-edges).
findings.suggestion: maxStepsPerTick budget (default 100 > 50-step funnel max) bounds per-tick graph traversal -> a loop without a MENU/Delay park fails fast (FUNNEL_STEP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED) instead of pinning a CPU. Covered by loop_without_wait_trips_step_budget IT.

notes: No new secrets, no crypto, no raw SQL (Mongo criteria parameterized via query builder). At-most-once CAS unchanged. No injection, XSS, or SSRF surface introduced. OWASP A01 IDOR is the principal risk and is correctly closed by subscriberId-scoped CAS.
